page: Amazon Web Services m6in.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server type driven by 3rd Gen Intel Xeon Scalable 8375C processors. It provides 64 physical cores (128 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled) running at 3.5 GHz on an x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, matching the standard general-purpose ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware flags confirm hardware-assisted virtualization (vmx), hardware cryptographic acceleration (AES, VAES, SHA-NI), and AVX-512 extensions including VNNI. It features no integrated GPUs and includes no local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded throughput and vector performance. In multi-core testing, the server achieved strong ratings in stress-ng (124,977.74) and Geekbench (17,532.0), accompanied by top-tier finishes in the PassMark CPU score (87,838.82) and extended instruction sets (108,708.43). In contrast, single-core benchmarks such as single-thread stress-ng (1,909.88) and Geekbench single-core (1,686.0) perform in the middle 50% category. Memory subsystem bandwidth reaches strong levels, registering 339.05 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 132.92 GB/sec for write operations.

Network infrastructure is a significant highlight, featuring a 200 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This high-capacity network pipeline complements strong benchmark outputs in I/O and network-reliant domains, including 112.88 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 75.37 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference achieves strong metrics during prompt processing across 135M (2,746.4 tokens/sec) and 7B models (199.72 tokens/sec), though text generation speeds settle into the average tier.

Because the server lacks local storage, operational costs and architecture depend on network-attached storage (EBS) performance over its 200 Gbps network fabric. The bare-metal design provides total hardware ownership without hypervisor overhead, delivering high resource density for enterprise workloads. Best-fit use cases include distributed in-memory caching tiers, large-scale Clang compilation jobs, high-throughput network-bound microservices, enterprise databases, and containerized virtualization clusters.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose server powered by dual Intel Xeon 8375C processors, offering 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs at 3.5 GHz alongside 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory. Built on an x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction extensions, the system features a dedicated baseline network bandwidth of 200 Gbps. It contains no local storage and no GPUs, necessitating network-attached storage architectures. In benchmarks, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core compute and extended instruction processing, backed by strong uncached memory bandwidth of 339.05 GB/sec reads and 132.92 GB/sec writes. While single-thread execution lands in the median range, high parallel throughput drives strong results in Redis operations (112.88M ops/sec) and static web serving (75.37 GB/sec). The m6in.metal is optimal for network-intensive enterprise workloads, bare-metal virtualization, distributed caching, and large compilation pipelines.
